metadata.note: The pre-lease passenger era of the Cincinnati Southern Railway, 1877-1881: the railroad the City of Cincinnati built and owned through the Trustees of the Cincinnati Southern Railway (Ferguson Act, 1869). The Trustees never ran trains; every year of service was operated by a separate company under licence or lease. Drawn here: the Cincinnati Southern Railway Company (licensee, Ludlow - Somerset, 23 Jul 1877 - 20 May 1879) and the Cincinnati Railroad Company (lessee, 21 May 1879 - 11 Oct 1881; Ludlow - Somerset throughout, plus the Ohio River bridge and Somerset - Chattanooga from 1880). Under CLAUDE.md Rule 4 each operator is its own feature and colour; the two Ludlow - Somerset features share identical geometry. From 12 Oct 1881 the line was leased to the Cincinnati, New Orleans & Texas Pacific and is drawn in queen_crescent.geojson (whose first segment was moved from 1880 to 1881 in the same change). Not drawn: Kentucky Central operation of Lexington - Nicholasville for the city, 11 Dec 1873 - 22 Jul 1877 (no confirmed passenger year for that operator); Cincinnati - Ludlow before 1880 (passenger use over the bridge not established); construction railheads south of Somerset 1878-1879 (no public passenger service found).
sources: ICC Valuation Reports v.37, Cincinnati Southern Railway (operating table; construction table): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Trains/ICC_valuations/Cincinnati_Southern_Railway

'Agreements for operating road / Cincinnati Southern Railway' (Cincinnati, 1881?), contents list - agreements of 3 Jul 1877, 8 Dec 1877, 19 May 1879, lease of 11 Oct 1881: https://sclqld.org.au/catalogue/records/41615
History of Hamilton County, ch. XV 'Railroads' (rootsweb transcription) - quoted via search results only; the page returned HTTP 403

J. Fowler passenger-station lists, branchline.uk Kentucky PDF line 65 (read directly 2026-10-27): https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/kentuckyrrs.pdf ; Tennessee PDF line 50 (via the CNO&TP research file)
not_yet_sourced: Who the Cincinnati Southern Railway Co. and the Cincinnati Railroad Co. were - independent capital or vehicles of men close to the Trustees. If either was a Trustees-controlled operating arm, the four features might reasonably merge into one 'Cincinnati Southern' feature 1877-1881. Until a source says so they are two operators.
The 1879 operator-change date: agreement 19 May 1879 (catalogue), operation from 21 May 1879 (ICC), '23 May 1879' (History of Hamilton County). Only the year is drawn.

The CNO&TP takeover: lease 'awarded' Sep 1881 / '7 Sep 1881' (secondary sources), CNO&TP incorporated 8 Sep 1881, lease dated 11 Oct 1881, operation from 12 Oct 1881 (ICC). The operating date is used.

Passenger trains over the Ohio River bridge into Cincinnati between 8 Dec 1877 and 8 Mar 1880 - not established, so the bridge feature starts 1880 and no 1877-1879 Cincinnati - Ludlow feature is drawn. The Cincinnati terminal of 1880-1883 is unlocated, so the approach north of the bridge is not drawn.
Any passenger service on partly completed sections south of Somerset (or north from Chattanooga) in 1878-1879 - not found; absence of evidence, nothing drawn.
The Cincinnati Enquirer's 'first lease lasted less than a year' against the ICC's 22 months (23 Jul 1877 - 20 May 1879) - perhaps counted from the 8 Dec 1877 agreement; unresolved.
Kentucky Central passenger service Lexington - Nicholasville for the city, 11 Dec 1873 - 22 Jul 1877 - Fowler has no 1875 or 1876 letter on the stretch; unconfirmed, omitted.
The last spike: 10 Dec 1879 near Robbins (Wikipedia) vs 11 Dec 1879 in Robbins Tunnel (Chattanoogan.com).

Sources not reached: the History of Hamilton County transcription (HTTP 403; wording known only from search-result quotes), the full text of 'Agreements for operating road' (licensed, Gale / Making of Modern Law), and Chronicling America. The agreements volume would settle the operator questions and the bridge question directly.
Headways and avg_speed_kmh are estimates; no 1877-1881 timetable has been checked.
The 1880-1881 Chattanooga approach over the Western & Atlantic from Boyce to the Union Depot is not drawn (final link not in OSM, depot site not pinned).
Original 1877-1881 alignments not drawn: Point Burnside (under Lake Cumberland since c.1950), the pre-1959 Rathole tunnels, and the Short Street alignment at Lexington.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py: 157.1 mi Ludlow - Somerset against ~157.8 mi documented (Fowler mileposts 3.2 at Ludlow and 161.0 at Somerset; the ICC records 147.00 mi built Ludlow - Lexington and Nicholasville - Somerset plus 13.00 mi Lexington - Nicholasville bought in). No straight-line legs. LATER ALIGNMENT: this is today's Norfolk Southern CNO&TP North District, not the 1877-1881 line. Known differences: (a) at Lexington the 1877-1881 trains used the ex-Lexington & Danville Short Street alignment; the trace follows the present-day line through Lexington, and only two short abandoned 'CNO&TP First District' fragments survive in OSM there; (b) the five-foot-gauge line of 1877 was standard-gauged in 1886 and has been rebuilt since, so curves and grade lines are those OSM maps today, not necessarily the 1877 ones. Where a 1877-1881 station sat off the present alignment is not established. The Ludlow end is the vertex nearest Ludlow, KY on the existing traced line, not a surveyed depot site.

segments.note: First passenger train Ludlow - Somerset 23 Jul 1877, run by the Cincinnati Southern Railway Company, a private 'organization of citizens' operating under licence from the Trustees of the Cincinnati Southern Railway (agreements of 3 Jul and 8 Dec 1877); the Trustees owned the line for the City of Cincinnati but never ran trains. The ICC operating table dates this company's operation 23 Jul 1877 - 20 May 1879, when the Cincinnati Railroad Co. took over (an operator change, not a service end - trains ran on). Somerset was railhead while the mountain section was finished. Five-foot gauge. Passenger service in 1877 is independently attested by 1877 Official Guide station names on this section in Fowler's Kentucky list ('Scott's' = later Wilmore, 'Tower's' = later High Bridge). Headway is an estimate (about two passenger trains a day each way), unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start 1877 and end 1879 are the ICC Valuation Reports v.37 operating table dates for the Cincinnati Southern Railway Co. (23 Jul 1877 - 20 May 1879), corroborated by the dated operating agreements and (via a search-result quote only) the History of Hamilton County; 1877 passenger service also shown by 1877 Official Guide names in branchline.uk Kentucky PDF line 65, read directly 2026-10-27. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Same trains, same track, new operating company: the Cincinnati Railroad Company, lessee of the Trustees under an agreement of 19 May 1879, operated from 21 May 1879 (ICC; the History of Hamilton County says 23 May) until 11 Oct 1881. On 12 Oct 1881 the CNO&TP took over under its lease of 11 Oct 1881, and the line is drawn from 1881 in queen_crescent.geojson. From 8 Mar 1880 this section was part of the through Cincinnati - Chattanooga service. Headway is an estimate (about two passenger trains a day each way), unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start 1879 and end 1881 are the ICC Valuation Reports v.37 operating table dates for the Cincinnati Railroad Co. (21 May 1879 - 11 Oct 1881), corroborated by the 19 May 1879 agreement in 'Agreements for operating road'. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 0.9 mi from Ludlow to the north (Ohio) end of the Cincinnati Southern Bridge (OSM ways 30735268/30735270, 'Cincinnati Southern Bridge'). The ICC gives 3.00 mi for 'Cincinnati, Ohio, to Ludlow, Ky., including bridge across the Ohio River'; the remaining ~2 mi on the Ohio side is deliberately NOT drawn, because the Cincinnati passenger terminal of 1880-1883 is unlocated (Fowler: '(where?)') and from April 1880 trains reached it over 1.08 mi of B&O Southwestern and 1.22 mi of CCC&StL track - drawing that approach would be invention. No straight-line legs. LATER ALIGNMENT: the bridge drawn is the structure OSM maps today; the crossing has been rebuilt since 1877 (date not checked here), and the 1877 structure's exact line is not separately mapped.

segments.note: The Cincinnati end of the through service, over the Cincinnati Southern Bridge across the Ohio River. The bridge was completed 8 Dec 1877, but no source found shows passenger trains crossing it before 1880, so 1880 is the earliest CONFIRMED year (through Cincinnati - Chattanooga passenger service from 8 Mar 1880; Fowler dates the first Cincinnati Southern passenger station in Cincinnati '(1880>1883)'), not a known opening date - passenger use from Dec 1877 is possible but unproven. Ends 1881 when the CNO&TP took over (12 Oct 1881). Drawn only to the bridge's north end: the 1880-1883 Cincinnati terminal is unlocated. Headway is an estimate (about two passenger trains a day each way), unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: end 1881 from the ICC Valuation Reports v.37 operating table; start 1880 is the earliest confirmed year, from Wikipedia (through passenger service began 8 Mar 1880) and Fowler's Cincinnati station date '(1880>1883)' (branchline.uk Kentucky PDF line 65, via the CNO&TP research file). Passenger use 1877-1879 not established. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py: 172.8 mi Somerset - Boyce (East Chattanooga) against 174.65 mi documented Somerset - Chattanooga (ICC). The documented figure runs to the Chattanooga terminal, a few miles beyond Boyce over Western & Atlantic track, so the fit is close. No straight-line legs. LATER ALIGNMENT, and badly so in places: (a) Burnside - the Cumberland River crossing and the town were relocated c.1950 for Lake Cumberland (Fowler: 'Former route until 1950'); the 1880-1881 line ran via Point Burnside (MP ~168.2), now under the reservoir, and the trace follows the post-1950 relocation. An unnamed, undated OpenHistoricalMap way leaving the line south of Burnside (start_date an arbitrary '1828') was not used because nothing identifies it as the original route. (b) The Rathole - the Southern Railway's 1959-1963 rebuild made numerous cuts and relocations to bypass tunnels; of the 27 original tunnels only #22 and #24 at Nemo and #25 and #26 at Oakdale remain on the line, and all but #25 are 1960s bores. The trace follows today's line, so between Somerset and Oakdale it is substantially the 1960s alignment, not the 1880 one; a few abandoned old-alignment fragments survive in OSM near Robbins and Sunbright (e.g. ways 919168687-919168690, 919168069-919168070) but are disconnected and were not stitched in. (c) Chattanooga - the trace runs from the Tennessee River crossing south to Boyce on today's NS Chattanooga Terminal District; the last ~1.2 mi into Boyce is the CNO&TP's own track that later paralleled the W&A, close beside it. CHATTANOOGA END: the line stops at Boyce, where the 1880 Cincinnati Southern met the Western & Atlantic (Chattanoogan.com, 2014). From there 1880-1881 trains ran over W&A track into downtown and the Union Depot (Fowler TN line 50, via the CNO&TP research file). That approach is NOT drawn: OSM has the W&A (CSX W&A Subdivision) out of Boyce, but the final link to the Union Depot site has been lifted and is not mapped, and the depot's exact site was not established; the end point is the vertex nearest Boyce (Nominatim hamlet, 0.3 km off).

segments.note: The mountain section ('the Rathole'), 27 original tunnels. Built by the Trustees and finished with the last spike in Dec 1879 (10 Dec near Robbins per Wikipedia; 11 Dec in Robbins Tunnel per Chattanoogan.com - conflict recorded, not resolved); first freight train into Chattanooga 21 Feb 1880 and first passenger train 8 Mar 1880, operated by the Cincinnati Railroad Co. until the CNO&TP took over on 12 Oct 1881. A '19 Dec 1879 first train' in one secondary source is taken to be a construction or inspection run and is not drawn; no public passenger service south of Somerset before 1880 was found. 1880 passenger service is independently attested by 1880 guide names on this section in Fowler (Oakdale as 'Hunnicutt', Upland as 'Summit', Whitley as 'Cumberland' in the 1880 Rand McNally guide; Stearns as 'Bridge Fork' in an 1880 Official Guide fare table). At Chattanooga the line met the Western & Atlantic at Boyce and used W&A track into the Union Depot, which is not drawn. Headway is an estimate (about two passenger trains a day each way), unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start 1880 (first passenger train into Chattanooga 8 Mar 1880) from Wikipedia and Chattanoogan.com, which agree; end 1881 from the ICC Valuation Reports v.37 operating table (CNO&TP from 12 Oct 1881); 1880 passenger service also shown by 1880 guide names in branchline.uk Kentucky PDF line 65 (read directly 2026-10-27) and Tennessee PDF line 50 (via the CNO&TP research file). Headway not sourced.
